chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'My father passed away and left two slave-girls whom he had manumitted conditionally (dabbara), and I am among those who testify to their manumission, and he has a large debt. What is your opinion?'
He said, 'May Allah be pleased with your father and raise him with Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). Paying off his debt is better for him, if Allah wills.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying the debts of a deceased person who left behind conditionally manumitted slaves?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms that settling the deceased's debts takes precedence over the immediate execution of manumission (*tadbir*), highlighting the Shia legal principle that financial obligations are a priority claim on the estate. The Imam’s invocation of divine pleasure for the father underscores the spiritual merit of debt repayment, linking material justice to the deceased's posthumous reward. This ruling balances the rights of creditors with the emancipation of slaves, ensuring that the estate is cleared of liabilities before distributing remaining assets to heirs or freeing servants.
